The issue reported states that `OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply(RealVector)` and `OpenMapRealVector.ebeDivide(RealVector)` return incorrect values when an entry of the specified `RealVector` is `NaN` or `Infinity`. The implementation of `ebeMultiply` and `ebeDivide` methods in the `OpenMapRealVector` class iterates through the entries of the vectors and performs element-wise multiplication and division, respectively.

In the implementation of `ebeMultiply`:
- The method loops through the entries of the vectors.
- For each entry, it calculates the product of the corresponding entries in the vectors.
- It correctly handles special cases where an entry in vector `v` is `NaN` or `Infinity` by setting the result entry to `NaN` or `Infinity` accordingly.

In the implementation of `ebeDivide`:
- The method also iterates through the entries of the vectors.
- For each entry, it calculates the division of the corresponding entries in the vectors.
- It does not handle the special case where an entry in vector `v` is `NaN` or `Infinity`, which can lead to incorrect results when dividing by zero or when dividing by `NaN` resulting in `NaN`.

The bug likely occurs in the `ebeDivide` method when dividing by zero or when dividing by `NaN` in the `v` vector. To fix this issue, proper handling of special cases where the divisor is `NaN` or `Infinity` should be added to the `ebeDivide` method.

Next, I will provide the methods that need to be fixed to address this issue.
```
org.apache.commons.math3.linear.OpenMapRealVector.ebeDivide(org.apache.commons.math3.linear.RealVector)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
